chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The dog of the Magians (Zoroastrians), you do not eat its game unless the Muslim takes it, teaches it, and sends it; and likewise the falcon, and the dogs of the People of the Covenant, and their falcons are permissible for Muslims to eat their game.
ai.seo_question: Is the game hunted by a Zoroastrian's dog permissible for Muslims to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies the fiqh of hunting by non-Muslims, distinguishing between the game of their dogs, which requires a Muslim to take and train it to ensure proper invocation, and their falcons, whose game is directly permissible. It reflects the Shia juristic view on the ritual purity and validity of hunting by Ahl al-Kitab, emphasizing the role of the Muslim in sanctifying the act when using their domesticated hunting animals.
